The TCP SYN Flood attack works by sending a high volume of SYN packets to a target system, which can overwhelm the system and lead to a denial of service (DoS). This attack exploits the TCP handshake process, where the attacker sends SYN requests without completing the handshake, causing the target to allocate resources for connections that are never established. As a result, the availability and functionality of the targeted system and network can be significantly reduced [Source 1].
